prompt:
Create a production illustration contact sheet for an image-first art style picker. One sheet, 4 columns by 3 rows, exactly 12 equally sized square panels, overall 4:3 canvas at 2048x1536 if possible. No margins or gaps; panel borders must align at exactly quarter-width and third-height. No text, numbers, labels, logos, or watermarks. Each panel is independent, with generous internal padding so the subject never crosses its boundaries. SAME SUBJECT in all panels: an original small fox courier with a satchel holding a flower, beside a tiny leafy plant. Keep this subject recognizable, but prioritize the DISTINCT visual medium in each panel. White/ivory paper background. The style differences must be obvious at thumbnail size; do not apply one uniform treatment to all panels. Styles in strict left-to-right top-to-bottom order:
1. Single-line figure: Describe the figure with a continuous directional contour.
2. Fine city lines: Use fine building contours and small human marks.
3. Brush-pen gestures: Use pressure changes to convey the weight of a gesture.
4. Dry-ink landscape: Let paper gaps interrupt dry strokes.
5. Stippled ink: Separate values through dot density.
6. Parallel hatching: Build shade with spacing between parallel strokes.
7. Crosshatched pen: Cross two stroke directions only in shadow areas.
8. Black silhouettes: Contrast large black masses with interior gaps.
9. Observation notebook: Explain form with contours and a few structural lines.
10. Bold contour: Separate heavy outlines from lighter interior detail.
11. Ink plus one color: Add one accent hue to black linework.
12. Open-space drawing: Connect parts of the subject through unmarked paper.
Professional expressive art samples, not UI mockups. Exactly 12 drawings in a perfectly regular 4x3 contact sheet.

Use case: illustration-story. Create one professional style-comparison contact sheet for an image-first art preset picker. Exactly 4 columns by 3 rows of equally sized square panels, edge to edge, 4:3 overall aspect ratio. No outer margins, gutters, text, IDs, labels, logos or watermarks. Very thin straight separators allowed at exact quarter-widths and third-heights. Each panel contains a fully framed independent drawing with internal padding. Same original subject across all panels: a small fox courier carrying a satchel and holding a flower beside a tiny leafy plant. The subject should stay recognizable, but vary the artistic treatment STRONGLY to demonstrate each specified style. Adapt closeups, props or scenery only when the named preset calls for it. Each of the 12 styles must visually stand apart. Light paper backgrounds except styles explicitly calling for dark backgrounds. Preserve clearly readable silhouette and material texture at thumbnail size. 
Strict left-to-right then top-to-bottom panel order:
1. Graphite form study. Use broad graphite planes to separate light and dark masses.
2. Fine pencil figures. Keep expressions in light lines with restrained shading.
3. Rough charcoal. Contrast soft dark masses with erased highlights.
4. Two-pencil palette. Separate the subject and supporting forms with two colors.
5. Layered colored pencil. Build color depth from layers of thin strokes.
6. Travel pencil notes. Keep essential shapes with uneven location-sketch lines.
7. Soft pastel blocks. Soften the edges of rounded color masses.
8. Thick crayon marks. Leave small paper gaps within broad waxy marks.
9. Scratched crayon. Reveal bright lines as if scratched through a dark wax layer.
10. Margin doodles. Use compact simple forms and relaxed linework.
11. Pale pencil nature. Describe leaf and stem directions with muted pencil marks.
12. High-contrast charcoal portrait. Preserve light facial planes against clustered shadows.
This is final website art, not a UI screenshot. Exactly twelve cells on a regular 4x3 sheet.
